<reason>B won a competitive debate by making “rather than rely on” a substitution test PRO never met: persistent campaigns, adversary-side collection, and lawful force still required a standing professional core, so reserves remained surge labor. A was stronger on talent, civilian terrain, and the motion’s “military” wording, but answering disruption with “existing authorities” and a civilian CERT left those units as the thing whose absence loses the contest. Clipped B speeches were a real cost, not enough to flip the clash.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s capture of A’s CERT/core and “existing authorities” concessions, especially that defender logs cannot see staging servers or multi-victim campaigns, recast the reserve as a supplement to standing sight and force.</best_rebuttal>
